label: miso 122b scope gate
definition: (PROBE — DISPATCH-LIVE / PRICE-INERT; promotion candidate NOT taken in-session) miso-122 arm B: the hybrid-cogen dark-fuel SCOPE GATE added to scripts/data/derive_chp_power_only_heat_rates.py. eGRID's plant-level CHP split cannot see a HYBRID cogen (a topping CC/CT train plus a direct-fired package boiler on one ORIS code), so 16.6 % of plant 55088 Dearborn's metered fuel — burned in three Other-boiler units with ZERO gross load — sat inside the topping rate charged to its CC_CHP (350 MW) and CT_CHP (165 MW) tranches, +16.6 % too dear. The gate removes it at CEMS unit grain: heat_rate = (PLHTIAN + CHPCHTI) * (1 - dark_fuel_share) / PLNGENAN, a SHARE not an MMBtu subtraction, zero free parameters, no threshold, strict no-op where absent. Applied rows: 55088 CC_CHP + CT_CHP 8.3465 -> 6.9573 (-16.6 %) and 10745 MCV 8.8243 -> 8.8160 (-0.09 %). RESULT: dispatch-live, price-inert — CC_CHP +0.36/+0.27/+0.52 TWh and CT_CHP +0.22 TWh/yr displacing CC_REGULAR, imports and COAL_PRB, but max zonal |dLMP| 0.049/0.039/0.075 $/MWh against a 0.10 pre-registered bar, so ZERO of three years clear it. Every gate passes (K1 artifact fidelity, K2 control byte-identity, K4 zero config delta, K5 span, K6 one-sided direction, P1-P6): nothing regresses, all nine criteria identical to the control, determination NOT-YET decided by the same C7 COAL_PRB shape FAIL this lever does not touch. Admissible on rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] ONLY and ships regardless of the residual. Evidence: FINDING-miso122-hybrid-cogen-scope-gate-2026-08-03.md, PREREG same date, _miso122_scope_gate_ab.json, PROBE-miso122-hybrid-cogen-scope-2026-08-03.txt.
market_story:
CC_CHP / CT_CHP (+0.36/+0.27/+0.52 and +0.22 TWh): Dearborn Industrial Generation is an industrial cogen selling into MISO-East off a topping CC+CT train, and its steam host also runs three package boilers fired directly for process heat. Those boilers make no electricity, so their fuel is not a cost of Dearborn's power -- a real merchant offering this plant into the day-ahead market bids the turbine train's own fuel burn, not the steam-house's. Pricing the whole facility's fuel against its MWh made the plant look 16.6 % less efficient than it is and pushed it up the stack behind units it genuinely beats. Corrected, it clears where a real bidder would put it.
CC_REGULAR (-0.19/-0.22/-0.31), import (-0.15/-0.11/-0.13) and COAL_PRB (-0.11/-0.06/-0.14): the mirror image, and the reason this is a re-ordering rather than an addition. A correctly-priced cogen displaces the marginal merchant combined cycle, the priced seam band and the PRB coal it now sits below -- which is exactly what a 515 MW efficiency correction should do to a stack, and why total system energy is unchanged.
Why price barely moves: 515 MW of re-ordering inside a ~100 GW market almost never changes the marginal unit. The demand-weighted lambda falls 0.03-0.06 $/MWh and no zone's lambda rises. That is the honest size of the effect and the run is not offered as a price-formation fix.
